title: The activity series: which metal wins

concepts.label: displacement reaction
concepts.definition: A metal dissolves as ions and forces another metal's ions out of solution as solid metal, e.g. Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu.

concepts.label: spontaneous reaction
concepts.definition: A reaction that goes by itself, downhill in energy, with no energy supplied from outside; its reverse is non-spontaneous and needs outside energy.

concepts.label: activity series
concepts.definition: The ranking of metals (plus hydrogen) by how readily they give electrons in water: Li, K, Ca, Na, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Ni, Sn, Pb, H, Cu, Ag, Au; a metal atom reacts with any ion on a lower rung.

concepts.label: acid (H⁺ in water)
concepts.definition: A solution rich in H⁺ ions, e.g. hydrochloric acid = HCl dissociated into H⁺ and Cl⁻; H⁺ can take electrons: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂.

concepts.label: metals vs acid (H₂ evolution)
concepts.definition: Metals above hydrogen in the series dissolve in acid and release hydrogen gas (M + nH⁺ → Mⁿ⁺ + n/2 H₂); metals below hydrogen do not.

concepts.label: noble metal
concepts.definition: A metal at the bottom of the series (silver, gold, platinum; copper borderline) that resists oxidation, survives ordinary acids and occurs in nature as metal.

concepts.label: energy bill: metal → dissolved ion
concepts.definition: The position in the series reflects three energy terms together: leaving the solid metal (cost), ionisation (cost) and hydration of the ion (payback).

concepts.label: hydration of an ion
concepts.definition: Water molecules cluster around a dissolved ion (oxygen ends toward a cation) and release energy, more for small, highly charged ions; this is why Li tops the series.

summary: Running example: the zinc strip in copper sulfate from Oxidation and reduction, extended to its reverse, then to Zn/Cu/Ag duels and a 14-metal ladder ('electrons fall from a metal atom to an ion on a lower rung') whose order is sorted from Chem.E0 without showing volts. Hydrogen gets a rung (metals in HCl), noble metals and the history of metal extraction mark the bottom, and a Li/Na/K energy bill (atomisation + ionisation − hydration) explains why ionisation energy alone mispredicts the order. Capstone: a mystery lab with six unlabelled metals (Mg, Zn, Fe, Pb, Cu, Ag) and their nitrate solutions; the learner runs dips, orders the letters and reveals the identities. Hooks for later lessons: the ladder picture maps directly onto the potential ladder, 'spontaneous = downhill' onto positive cell voltage, and 'force it uphill' onto electrolysis.
